previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of systolic heart failure, COPD, atrial fibrillation, and alcohol dependence was admitted for nausea, vomiting, throat pain, and abdominal discomfort following a heavy alcohol binge shortly after a recent hospital discharge. He was diagnosed with alcoholic gastritis and mild pulmonary edema, with no evidence of acute cardiac ischemia, pancreatitis, or intra-abdominal pathology on imaging. He was treated with IV fluids, antiemetics, acid-suppression therapy, and symptomatic relief for throat discomfort, and gradually advanced to a regular diet. His kidney function and electrolyte abnormalities improved with supportive care. Alcohol withdrawal was managed with thiamine and diazepam as needed, and he remained stable. He expressed interest in future alcohol treatment but declined immediate transfer, opting to stay with his sister post-discharge. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged and all home medications restarted.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with hx of CAD and multiple PCI who presents with chest pain 
and EtOH withdrawal. Admitted to ICU for phenobarbital loading 
protocol. Briefly, he was loaded with phenobarbital, and upon 
stabilization he was called out to the floor on ___. His 
floor course was c/b hypotensive and afib with RVR. He 
eventually left the hospital Against Medical Advice on ___.  


ACTIVE ISSUES 
==============

# AMA. The patient ultimately left the hospital Against Medical 
Advice on ___. The patient was AOx3 and had capacity to make 
this decision upon evaluation. The risks and benefits of leaving 
AMA, which included but were not limited to worsening alcohol 
withdrawal, continued chest pain, and death, were discussed and 
he expressed his understanding of these risks. 

# EtOH dependence/withdrawal: His last drink was ___ @ 
10:30 pm. No history of DT or seizures, states that he ""gets 
shaky"" when withdrawing from alcohol. Got 40mg Diazepam in 5 
hours and then loaded with 720mg phenobarbital. He required a 
360mg phenobarbital rescue load, and was treated for additional 
symptoms with 0.2mg clonidine TID. Upon transfer to the floor 
clonidine was discontinue and he was continued on the oral 
phenobarbital taper. He left Against Medical Advise in the 
middle of his phenobarbital taper.  

# Atypical Chest Pain: On admission, patient had chest pain in 
the ED. It is unclear if this was consistent with prior MI 
symptoms. Troponins on admission were flat at .02, likely in the 
context of tachycardia of likely ETOH withdrawal. Troponins were 
trended and remained flat at <0.01. EKG from the ED consistent 
with prior EKGs without new ST or T wave changes. He was treated 
for his chest pain with a GI cocktail given his response to GI 
cocktail in the past for gastritis pain. As his pain was 
controlled with GI cocktail and his troponins did not elevate, 
heparin was not initiated. On the floor, he experienced 
recurrent chest pain described as sharp twinges of pain 
overlying the front of his chest. Repeated troponins were 
checked and were <0.01. EKG was unchanged from prior in ___ 
and in the ED. He was briefly started on heparin gtt overnight 
for chest pain but this was discontinued after <24 hours given 
negative troponins and low concern for ACS. Per the patient, his 
chest pain was unchanged from his chronic chest pain. This chest 
pain was unrelieved by cardiac catheterization in the past. It 
was decided given that this was not likely ACS to not pursue 
cardiac catheterization. Furthermore, he is non compliant with 
medications so in the event of him needing a stent, there was 
concern for medication nonadherence and risk for instent 
rethrombosis. He was offered a variety of medications to help 
treat his pain, which he declined. He refused to trial SL nitro 
given side effect of headache. Chest pain was at his baseline 
when he decided to leave Against Medical Advice.  

# A-fib: CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (CHF, HTN). Arrived to CVICU in AFib 
RVR to 150s, remained normotensive, mentating at baseline. Rate 
controlled with 5mg IV metoprolol bolus. AFib likely due to 
recent noncompliance with home metoprolol (12.5 Q6 per recent 
discharge regimen) and in the setting of alcohol withdrawal. 
Interaction between rivaroxaban and phenobarbital noted, however 
given CHADS2-VASc = 2 and low/no suspicion for MI he was not 
bridged. Rivaroxaban was held and should not be restarted until 
at least 1 week after the last dose of phenobarbital. On the 
floor, the patient experienced another afib with RVR episode 
again responsive to IV metoprolol 5mg and reinitiation of home 
dosing metoprolol tartrate 12.5mg q6. The patient decided to 
leave Against Medical Advise. He was advised to continue taking 
metoprolol (succinate 50mg daily) at home and that he should NOT 
start taking rivaroxaban until at least 1 week after leaving the 
hospital.  

# Hypotension. On the floor, he had episodes of SBPs ___ 
several times ___, with occasional lightheadedness and chest 
pain (below) likely iatrogenic in setting of anti-hypertensive 
medications continued after being called out from MICU where 
they were needed to treat HTN from alcohol w/d and diuresis in 
setting of limited PO intake. Blood pressure stabilized s/p 
discontinuation of all anti-HTN (lisinopril, Lasix, 
spironolactone). He left Against Medical Advice. We were able to 
set up an appointment with a resident at ___ for him to be seen 
within 1 week where he should have blood pressure rechecked to 
decided on reinitiation of previous anti-hypertensive 
medications. 

# Acute on chronic systolic heart failure: There was e/o mild 
pulmonary edema on admission CXR, with some dyspnea. He was 
treated with intravenous Lasix to reach a goal of net negative 
fluid balance. On the floor, he became hypotensive, likely 
iatrogenic in the setting of overdiuresis in the ICU and 
continuation of home anti-HTN medications (that per his sisters 
report he was likely not taking at home given non compliance 
with medications). Anti-HTN meds, including Lasix, were held on 
discharge in the setting of recent hypotensive events. Given 
that he left Against Medical Advice, we were unable to provide 
recommendations for timing of restarting these medications. An 
appointment was set up with a resident at ___ within 1 week of 
discharge to help with management of these issues.
